Thank you for the update. Now I need to ask about the risks. What is your biggest worry?
The environmental license. If the agency delays it, the tender will move to next year.
And if that happens, what will you do?
We will ask for a new schedule. The contract allows it, so there will be no penalty.
What about traffic? Our model assumes the numbers from 2024.
If traffic falls, the concession will have a shortfall. That is why we have asked for a state guarantee.
Honestly, if the rules were more predictable here, my board would approve this in one meeting.
I agree. If I were the regulator, I would publish the decisions earlier. For now, we reduce the uncertainty with the contract.

For every project, I write three scenarios for the board. The first one is the base case: if everything happens as planned, what will the returns be? The second one is the bad case. For a toll road, for example, if traffic falls by ten percent, will the concession still pay its debts? And the third one is the worst case. If traffic falls by twenty percent, the concession will have a shortfall, and we will need a guarantee. People think the board wants to see a perfect project. It doesn't. It wants to see a clear plan for each scenario.

People sometimes ask me what I would change if I were a regulator. My answer is always the same. If I were a regulator, I would publish the calendar of decisions for the whole year. Investors don't need every decision to be good for them. They need to know when the decision will come. If they knew the calendar, there would be less uncertainty, and they would accept lower returns. And here is the part people forget. When investors ask for higher returns, the users pay for it with higher tariffs. So the real cost of uncertainty is on the users.

The state government has confirmed that its tender for a new metro line received no bids. Not one. Construction companies and foreign funds had shown interest last year, but in the end nobody made an offer. According to three companies, the problem was the tariff, which was too low, and the fact that there was no state guarantee. The government now says that if it changes the rules, it will open the tender again in six months. Analysts are not so sure. If the new rules are ready before the elections, they say, investors might come back. If not, the project could wait another two years.
